newsitem.title: USA: Coleman hit by weak Japanese sales.
newsitem.headline: Coleman hit by weak Japanese sales.

text.p: Shares of Coleman Co Inc, which makes camping and related recreation products, fell 2-1/4 to 14-1/4 on Friday over concerns about weaker sales in Japan, an analyst said.

On Thursday Denver-based Coleman said it expected a small loss for the third quarter due to several factors, including bad camping weather this summer in the United States and lower than expected sales in Japan.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell C.J. Lawrence analyst Peter Barry said he cut his rating on Coleman to hold from buy, citing concern over sales in Japan.
Barry lowered his earnings estimate for 1997 to $1.08 per share from $1.27.
Barry said Japanese sales, which account for about 10 percent of total Coleman sales, had been a "major growth driver" when weather problems in the United States came up in the past.

Coleman spokesman Charles McIlwaine said the recent European acquisition of Camping Gaz would be accretive to earnings in 1997 and, on an annualized basis, would start contributing $180-$220 million to revenues.
But Barry said he expects the 1997 contribution from Camping Gaz to be modest, with improvement coming in 1998.
